summary: Takashi Maeda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University. He was attested as a lecturer at Taisho University in 1995 and 2006.

Takashi Nakao (1931–2020) specialized in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. Educated at Rissho University and Tokyo University of Education, he held posts at Bunkyo University Women's College, Rissho University (emeritus professor, 1979–2002), and the Society of Japanese Historical Documents.

Takashi Ogawa is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Peking University, and the University of Tokyo. He became an assistant professor at Komazawa University in 1991.
Takashi Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Hosei University. He was attested as an assistant professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto in 2003.
Takatoshi Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Komazawa University, attested in 1978–1981 and 1991.
Takatoshi Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ryukai Mano in 1979 and served as a researcher at the Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute, Taisho University, attested in 1978.

Takatsugu Hayashi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at the University of Delhi. He held posts at Tohoku University (attested 1997), Sendai National College of Technology (attested 2008), and Hosen Gakuen College (attested 2015).

Takayasu Higuchi (1919–2015) studied at Kyoto University and worked in history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian, and Buddhist studies. He was a professor at Kyoto University (~1968–1983) and directed the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Sen-oku Hakuko Kan, and the Institute of Silk Road Studies.

Takayasu Kimura is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. He served as a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1969–1978) and held posts at Taisho University and the Institute of Contemporary Mission of Shingon Buddhism Buzan-ha.
Takayasu Suzuki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University, attested in 2014–2015.

Takayoshi Kamei (1886–1977) was a history, archaeology, and Japanology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Ibaraki University (~1949–1957), and Seisen University (~1957–1967), and taught Hajime Nakamura.

Takayoshi Namikawa is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at Bukkyo University. He was a professor (appointed 1981) and later emeritus professor (2018) at Bukkyo University, also holding posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University and Hokkaido University.

Takayuki Hirosawa is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. His career includes posts at Taisho University through 1991 and as professor attested in 2014.

Takehiro Sueki (1921–2007) was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1941–1944). He held academic posts at the University of Electro-Communications (~1957–1965), the University of Tokyo (~1965–1982), and Toyo University (~1982–1992).

Takeo Hibino (1914–2007) was a Sinologist and historian who studied at Kyoto University. He worked at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities and the university itself (1948–1977), later becoming a professor at Otemon Gakuin University and professor and president at Otemae University.
Takeo Warita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi.

Takeshi Fujii is an Indologist and historian who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Delhi. He spent his career at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, advancing from assistant in 1987 to professor and emeritus professor (2021).

Takeshi Karashima (1903–1967) was a Sinologist who studied at Yamaguchi Higher School and Tokyo Imperial University. He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1931–1945), Sagami Women's University, Showa Women's University, and Kamakura's library.

Takeshi Umehara (1925–2019) worked in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies, studying at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held posts at Ryukoku, Ritsumeikan, Kyoto City University of Arts, the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (1987–1995), and the Institute of Technologists.

Takeshiro Kuraishi (1897–1975) was a Sinology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He was a professor at Kyoto University (~1939–1949), worked at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1958), and served as president of the Chinese Linguistics Research Society (~1957–1968).
